Title: Need help with this Gangrel deck

Messages.Author: AceWolf
Messages.Body:

Can anyone suggest me some improvements? Or strategy to play it best?

And I get ousted from the game by running out of resources very quickly.I usually start by waking Ingrid to get more transfers. Messages.Author: Timo
Messages.Body:
Yes you understand correctly but what is your goal with this deck ?

Bringing out all 3 vampires and destroying your opponnent's vampires with the additional benefit of gaining a lot of pool ?

Doing all that seems cool on paper but it is a somewhat fragile strategy for different reasons :

the first is a lot of moving parts :
- having a big vampire out (justicar and inner circle are not cheap)
- passing an alastor political action (need to not be blocked and have enough votes)
- passing an anathema political action (again !)
- entering combat with said target
- empty the target

the second problem is no less problematic :
- burning your opponent vampires doesn't give you VP (which is how you win)

and the last problem is what I consider to be the last nail that broke the camel back :
- not all your opponents will have big juicy vampires you will want/need to destroy : some will have only small vampires and other mainly allies and small vamires in big numbers or any number of allies will be problematic for an alastor deck ( the 2 ancillas are a good start).

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> the first is a lot of moving parts :
> - empty the target
>
Especially with only 2 Dog Packs, you will not manage to burn vampires playing Strike: Combat Ends reliably. Since you need the pool to survive, you may die quickly, especially with no crypt acceleration and if you plan to bring Ingrid out first (who cannot play Alastor).
>
> the second problem is no less problematic :
> - burning your opponent vampires doesn't give you VP (which is how you win)
>
That's the main problem.

The 25th anniversary works the opposite: bring Stanislava out first because she can play everything at superior (so if you have an aggressive predator, you can still play your cards at their best), and most importantly, she can Govern down to bring out other vampire for a discount. And she can deflect, meaning a higher chance of survival.

I'd suggest you give it a try to compare how the two decks behave.

Alastor / Anathema is not bad, but 1/ probably with a different crypt that can play Psyche! (only Stanislava would be able to do with this crypt) 2/ you still need a plan to oust your prey.

Messages.Author: smeeag
Messages.Body:
As described below, this deck have many moving parts on the way to success:
- Big caps
=> Slow influencing especially without governs, zillahs, highway

- Your combat significantly rely on weapon from Alastor, but it's also tricky.
=> You may you have tiny stealth module. Not required to be a wall, just telepathic misdirection is enough.
=> High chances not to draw it in the first few turns at all.
=> Vote lock is also real, with highcaps (enemies will influence all they want also) + no vote gain.

- Anathema pool gain is OK, but have it flaws: it's weak vs low-caps and if you got blocked by other minion (not only vampire, imagine nocturn / legionnaire) you (1) got no pool (2) lost a turn for 10-cap vampire requiring multiturn setup.

- The plan "weaken the predator by turn 6 in the perfect scenario" then bleed the prey with base bleeds of avg. < 2 is very questionable, because... there are 3 other players on the table and your prey were free to do anything (no pool / combat pressure from you).
